newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crude prices up in late Asia, wet barrels immobile.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices up in late Asia, wet barrels immobile.

text.p: Crude oil prices inched up during late Asian trading hours on Monday, traders said. The market was quiet due to the absence of regional traders as many were away for the Chinese New Year's holiday, they said.
"It's very, very dead," one trader said.
They said there was no fresh news to provide direction.
At 0805 GMT, March NYMEX light crude on the ACCESS after-hours system stood at $22.33/22.39, compared with last Friday's New York close of $22.23.
On SIMEX, March cash Brent was indicated at $20.98/21.15, a touch firmer than the IPE settlement of $20.95.
Crude oil prices declined in overseas markets last Friday. NYMEX light crude tumbled due to diminished demand for refined products, and the slump also pressured IPE Brent crude oil futures.
In the physical market, Tokyo traders were mostly sidelined with their counterparts in Asia away for the holidays.
Traders said most Middle Eastern crude oil barrels for March have been placed, but that it was still too early to discuss April barrels.
There was some unconfirmed talk that a few Abu Dhabi grades might still be available for March, but no indications were available and interest in the cargoes appeared lacklustre.
The premium for April Middle Eastern crude barrels is excepted to become softer, but active discussion is not expected to take place until later this week at the earliest, traders said.
